title: CommerceFabric
shortDescription: A cloud-native e-commerce platform exploring production-style microservices, distributed communication, resilience, and Azure infrastructure.
overview: CommerceFabric is a production-inspired distributed e-commerce platform built to explore the architectural trade-offs involved in designing and operating independently deployable microservices. It covers service boundaries, data ownership, synchronous and asynchronous communication, caching, resilience, identity, infrastructure as code, and automated deployment on Azure.
problem: Design a realistic distributed system without allowing individual services to become tightly coupled, while handling cross-service workflows, independent data ownership, authentication, transient failures, and deployment as the platform grows.
solution: I separated users, products, and orders into independently deployable ASP.NET Core services with database-per-service persistence. REST handles synchronous communication, while RabbitMQ and Azure Service Bus demonstrate asynchronous event-driven workflows. Redis reduces repeated cross-service lookups, Polly handles transient failures, Microsoft Entra ID provides identity, and traffic is routed through Azure API Management and Ocelot.
outcome: The finished platform demonstrates the trade-offs involved in building a cloud-native distributed system: independently deployable services, eventual consistency, fault isolation, resilient communication, centralized API governance, and automated infrastructure and application delivery on Azure.
highlights: Designed independently deployable services with clear ownership of business logic and persistence
Implemented asynchronous workflows with Azure Service Bus Topics, RabbitMQ, and dead-letter handling
Used Redis caching and Polly resilience policies to reduce coupling and tolerate transient failures
Provisioned Azure infrastructure with Bicep and deployed containerized services to AKS
Built GitHub Actions pipelines covering testing, containerization, ACR publishing, infrastructure deployment, and AKS releases
Integrated Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft Graph, Azure API Management, and Ocelot for identity and API routing
